extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages designed for a word prediction task where the target word is hard to guess from the last sentence alone but becomes easy with the broader discourse context. It is intended to test models' ability to use broad context for text understanding.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built from the Book Corpus by selecting passages with a context and target sentence; the corpus was duplicate-removed and filtered for potentially offensive material, then novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions, and LAMBADA was built from the latter.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus novels; after preprocessing, the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The task was to guess the last word of the target sentence (the target word). The context size was chosen in a pilot study, and the target word was constrained to be the last word of the sentence to make the task more natural for human subjects.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA, while common nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented compared to the input distribution. The dataset also tends to include target words that are strongly cued in the broader discourse, often because the target word or its lemma appears in the context.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The task is challenging for automated models and preliminary experiments found that existing language modeling architectures did not come close to human performance. The dataset is also constructed from unpublished novels, which reduces usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources; many items can be guessed from local sentence context only, so broad discourse context is not always necessary.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper does not discuss broader social impacts beyond noting that the corpus was filtered to remove potentially offensive material.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Designed as a word prediction benchmark for language modeling and to test language modeling architectures, including systems with longer-term contextual memory. The authors indicate models should be trained on raw text from the training partition, with LAMBADA built from the development+testing partition.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We randomly divided the novels into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
